subject: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlaspayments.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps - Atlas Payments

Hi Samir/Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier today - good discussion. Quick recap and proposed success criteria for the POC/trial so we can align on what "success" looks like:

- Scope: End-to-end inference for payments fraud scoring integrated via Redwood API (text + embeddings) against a sample of historical transactions you provide.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - Latency: p95 <= 200ms (endpoint; from request to first-token). If Atlas prefers tighter, we can target p95 <= 150ms on Dedicated.
  - Throughput: sustain 500 req/s with bursts to 1,000 req/s for short windows.
  - Cost: <= $0.0008 per token (estimate with batching & quantized model).
  - Quality: >= 90% pass-rate on your sample evaluation set (we'll agree on labeling rules and eval prompts).
- Evaluation plan: two-week trial. Week 0: instrumentation + baseline, Week 1: synthetic load + model tuning, Week 2: live traffic / A/B comparisons. We'll run automated evals daily and produce a short report at the end.
- Ownership:
  - Atlas: provide sample dataset, business success criteria, and point-of-contact for engineering (Samir/CloudOps).
  - Redwood: SE lead (Marissa) will run instrumentation, provide test harness and baseline report; Jordan will oversee success criteria and contract/next steps.

Next steps:
1) Confirm if you want p95 target of 150ms vs 200ms (we can plan for Dedicated if 150ms).
2) Share sample dataset and expected TPS/traffic shape (CSV or S3 link).
3) Kickoff meeting: propose Tue 16 Jun 2026 10:00am PT for a 30-min kickoff (instrumentation checklist + data handoff).

I've attached a short POC plan and dropped the drive link below. If the success criteria above look good, we'll lock the plan and schedule kickoff.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-redwood-poc-plan

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@atlaspayments.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps - Atlas Payments

Thanks Jordan - that's a helpful recap. Two quick notes:
- We were hoping to aim for p95 <= 150ms if possible; latency is a competitive requirement for us. If that requires Dedicated config, we can discuss cost tradeoffs.
- Can you confirm how you count tokens (prompt + response?) and whether embeddings are billed separately? Also need clarity on data retention for the trial.

Happy to meet on Tue 16th - 10am PT works for me. Priya and our CloudOps team will share sample data ahead of time.

- Samir
Director, Engineering
Atlas Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlaspayments.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps - Atlas Payments

Thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications and how we'll measure things:

- Token counting: Redwood counts tokens as prompt + response (we'll provide the tokenizer tool). Embeddings are billed per-embedding call - we'll separate those in the report.
- Latency measurement: we'll measure end-to-end server-side p95 from request-receipt to first-token emitted and also provide client-side timing hooks if you want. We'll push metrics to a shared Prometheus endpoint or provide a dashboard link.
- Test harness: we'll run a baseline (no batching) and a tuned run (batching, cached prefixes, quantization). For p95 150ms target, Dedicated instances with int8 quantization + tuned kernel selection is usually required for models in the 70B range.
- Instrumentation checklist attached - please ensure CloudOps can open a port for our test runner and provide an S3 link for the dataset.

We'll prep the baseline report within 3 business days of kickoff. Looking forward to Tue.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: poc-instrumentation-checklist.md

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Success Criteria & Next Steps - Atlas Payments

Great - locking Tue 16 Jun 2026 10:00am PT for a 30-min kickoff. Agenda: introductions, data handoff, instrumentation checklist review, immediate blockers and access.

Samir - can you share the sample dataset or S3 link and an estimate of steady-state TPS and peak TPS? Also confirm who on CloudOps will be our technical contact.

If no blockers, we'll proceed with instrumentation during week of 6/16 and aim to have baseline report by 6/19.

Thanks,
Jordan
